title: ReSIDS adaptation event
description: One observability event emitted by the ReSIDS adaptation plane. Served as an element of GET /events (REST pull) and pushed to the monitor as CoAP telemetry (values object).

seq.description: Monotonic, unique event sequence number (continues across runs).

ts.description: Event timestamp, ISO-8601 UTC with microseconds (REST). When pushed as CoAP/ThingsBoard telemetry it is converted to epoch milliseconds in the enclosing envelope.

round.description: Federation round in which the event occurred.

from_mode.description: Previous aggregation mode (architecture_change only; null otherwise).

to_mode.description: New aggregation mode (architecture_change only; null otherwise).

reason.description: Cause of the event. architecture_change: node_failure | recovery | scheduled | intrusion | commanded | autonomous_fallback. node_failure: node_failure. node_recovery: recovery. node_isolated: intrusion. Only 'node_failure' while in federated mode is acted on autonomously (fail-fast FL->GL); every other cause is monitor-governed. The last two distinguish the outcome of the FL-pending race under the monitor_commanded policy (docs/COMMANDS.md 4.1): 'commanded' = the monitor's set_mode arrived within the deadline D; 'autonomous_fallback' = D expired first and the node self-protected.

failed_nodes.description: Logical node indices identified as failing (authoritative on node_failure; context on architecture_change).

active_nodes.description: Node indices participating this round, or null when all are active.

attack.description: intrusion_detected only: detected attack class/type (e.g. 'injection', 'masquerade_fake_fault'); null otherwise.

k_votes.description: intrusion_detected only: number of concurring specialists (the k in k-of-n) that raised the alarm — the corroboration strength.

n_flags.description: intrusion_detected only: number of samples/flows flagged in this round/window (alarm volume).

source_node.description: intrusion_detected only: attributed emitter node (e.g. from the GOOSE/SV source), or null when attribution is unavailable (typical in v2).

detector_specialists.description: intrusion_detected only: indices of the SPECIALISTS (boosters) in the local pool that fired. Not nodes: every node holds the same diffused union and reaches the same verdict, so what varies is which specialists fired.

recovered_nodes.description: node_recovery only: logical node indices that came back.

mode.description: Aggregation mode in effect for this event, so the monitor never infers state.

n_active.description: Number of active nodes when the event was emitted (len(active_nodes)).

window_start.description: Start of the evaluated traffic window, from the GOOSE/SV frame timestamps (synthetic epoch under simulation). Distinct from ts, which is the emission instant.

window_end.description: End of the traffic window, exclusive.

window_samples.description: Samples scored in the window - the denominator for n_flags.

decided_by.description: Who took the ACTION. Present only on events that ARE an action: architecture_change and node_isolated. Pure observations (node_failure, node_recovery, intrusion_detected) carry no decision and omit it. autonomous is reserved for the single autonomous action in the system - the fail-fast FL->GL triggered by node inactivity; every other action (further losses in GL, intrusion-driven isolation, the GL->FL return) is monitor or operator.

command_id.description: The command that caused this action, when one did (docs/COMMANDS.md). Present only where decided_by is 'monitor' or 'operator'; null or absent on an autonomous action, which no command caused. This field is what closes the loop between the two surfaces: the command result can be lost in transit, so the EVENT carrying command_id is the authoritative commit record, and the monitor correlates on it rather than trusting its HTTP response.

examples.detail: monitor-commanded isolation after corroborated alarms attributed to node 9
